solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Masterstroke, having attachment to Bond?

parts.note: a coup is a brilliant, successful stroke
to have something on is to be wearing it, so having can give the little word on

explanation.surface: A brilliant idea fixed onto James Bond, the spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' with its capital looks like 007, but it is a financial bond; old bearer bonds came with detachable vouchers clipped off to claim interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper bonds once carried detachable interest vouchers, torn off and presented for payment, so the voucher is a literal attachment.

clue.text: Line of credit given with no difficulty

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts
ease is the absence of difficulty

explanation.surface: A bank offers a line of credit without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line of credit' reads as one banking phrase, but 'Line' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold mark or wrinkle is a line, as on paper or a face.

clue.text: Rash song supporting primitive movement that can't be controlled

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath, so the song comes after the rest

parts.note: ur- is a prefix meaning original or primitive, as in Ur-text
a tic is an involuntary twitch
an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: A hasty song backing some primitive, uncontrollable artistic movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like an adjective (reckless) but is the noun, a skin eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Urticaria is the medical name for hives, an itchy skin eruption.

clue.text: Going places? Stupidly, he put 'No'

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it in a muddled way, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly answered no when asked if he was heading somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone improving or rising in fortunes is said to be going places, an idiom for prospering.

clue.text: Get used to current trade

parts.note: AC is alternating current
custom means business or patronage, as in giving a shop your custom

explanation.surface: Learn to live with the way business is done these days.
explanation.definitionFit: To habituate someone to something is to make them familiar with it through repetition.

clue.text: Cohabitation of Tory with young pup when old

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the party also called Tory
a cub is a young animal, and also a raw youngster
being old is being in age, advanced in years

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician living with a young whippersnapper in his dotage.
explanation.definitionFit: Living together as a couple without being married is the old legal sense of this word.

clue.text: Excerpt from Rasputin, framed as below

indicators.note: Excerpt from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clipping about the Russian mystic Rasputin, displayed in a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used in texts to refer the reader to a later passage, meaning see further down.

clue.text: Kick bishop? That is human

parts.note: to toe a ball is to kick it with the toe
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: Kicking a bishop: only human, really.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes Pope's line 'To err is human, to forgive divine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope's proverb says making mistakes is part of being a person, so the phrase is what is human.

clue.text: I am in troubled market — keep going without progressing

indicators.note: the short form of I am is placed inside the rearranged letters
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of market are stirred up

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: A trader confesses to being stuck in a troubled market, merely treading water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' gives the scramble MARKTE, which 'in' then opens up for the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers mark time by marching on the spot; figuratively it means waiting without advancing.

clue.text: Property of French art gallery

parts.note: ès is French for of the or in, as in docteur ès lettres
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A painting owned by a French gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Land and buildings held by an owner make up a landed holding, so the word means property.

clue.text: Maintenance person needs space, hoisting machine constantly

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
a gin is a hoisting device with a tripod and winch
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: The repair man needs room, his crane working nonstop.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic who services and repairs equipment is a maintenance technician.

clue.text: Parisian's goodness, offering useable mobile with admission for clubs by right

indicators.note: the rearranged letters let the next pieces in, taking them inside
mobile means movable, so the letters of useable shift around

parts.note: C is clubs in card notation

explanation.surface: A Frenchman exclaims about a phone that is easy to use, letting a club in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' gives the scramble SAEBLEU, and 'with admission for' lets clubs and right in after its second letter. 'mobile' reads as a phone, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The French exclamation is a mild oath, like an English speaker crying 'my goodness!'

clue.text: Political organisation's social work changing priorities?

indicators.note: the order of the two pieces is swapped, so the work comes first and the social second

parts.note: labour is work
a social is a party or gathering

explanation.surface: A group's social work is shifting its priorities.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in clue order the pieces give PARTY LABOUR; swapping them gives the British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Labour Party is a major political party, one of the two that have long dominated UK government.

clue.text: Prime trees will take time

parts.note: firs are conifer trees

explanation.surface: Top-quality trees take a while to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime and its synonym both mean foremost or top-ranking.

clue.text: What some politicians believe in; populace being taken in remains confused

indicators.note: the people's word is absorbed inside the muddled letters
confused means mixed up, so the letters of remains are muddled

parts.note: the populace is the general public

explanation.surface: The people are fooled and the wreckage left behind is a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' gives the scramble REANISM, and 'being taken in' opens it after its second letter for the people.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of a state with an elected head rather than a monarch hold this political creed.

clue.text: Illiterate Italian lady with letter that's moving succeeded after all

indicators.note: the letter for succeeded is shifted from its place
the shifted letter goes to the very end, after everything else

parts.note: signora is Italian for a married lady
mu is a Greek letter
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: An unlettered Italian woman whose letter is touching ended up a success.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGNORA + MU gives SIGNORAMU; its opening S moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiterate as a noun means an uneducated person, an ignorant one.

clue.text: Lloyd Webber work sent back by censor with separate notes

indicators.note: returning the title means reading that musical's name backwards

parts.note: Cats is a musical by Andrew Lloyd Webber
Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor and is known as Cato the Censor

explanation.surface: A Lloyd Webber show is returned by a censor with jumpy notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is a musical direction for detached, clipped notes, each cut short.

clue.text: Failing stamina? Turn to alchemy

indicators.note: failing means breaking down, so the letters fall apart and reassemble

explanation.surface: Running out of energy, someone resorts to magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemists sought to change base metals into gold, so the change of one substance into another is the art itself.

clue.text: Establish Italian restaurants?

parts.note: the first word read upwards, as in a down entry, gives trats, informal for trattorias

explanation.surface: Open some trattorias.
explanation.walkthrough: Trat is informal for a trattoria, a simple Italian restaurant; the answer's first word written up the grid spells it.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up a business is to launch or found it.

clue.text: Popular to keep chapter end as motto

indicators.note: the popular word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to die is to come to an end

explanation.surface: A fashionable choice to preserve the chapter's ending as a slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: 'I serve' in German is the Prince of Wales's heraldic motto.

clue.text: Apply to get free access code

parts.note: to apply something is to use it
rid means freed of something, as in being rid of a pest

explanation.surface: Submit an application to obtain free entry codes.
explanation.definitionFit: A login name identifying a person to a computer system serves as an access credential.

clue.text: Prisoner and Georgia dance in chains

parts.note: con is short for convict
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A convict and a Georgian dance in shackles, like a chain gang.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin American dance is performed in a long line of people holding each other's waists.

clue.text: Relative's base in French city

indicators.note: the base letter goes inside the name of the city

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A relation's home is a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: Large numbers of appeals needing god's intervention

indicators.note: intervening means coming between, so the god goes into the middle of the appeals

parts.note: pleas are appeals or entreaties
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: Many prayers require divine intervention.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or glut, so several of them are large quantities.

clue.text: Cheeky, diving into a river opening

indicators.note: the cheeky word plunges inside the other pieces

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
pert means saucy or cheeky

explanation.surface: A cheeky swimmer jumps into a river opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole or gap, such as a camera's lens opening, is the meaning.

clue.text: Lighting controller's not so clever

definitions.meaning: a switch that lowers a lamp's brightness

explanation.surface: The lighting technician isn't very bright.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that reduces brightness, and the comparative of an adjective for slow-witted.

clue.text: What a gull does perhaps above French country

parts.note: over means above
pays is French for country

explanation.surface: A seagull flies over France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gull' looks like the seabird, but here it is a dupe, an easily cheated person.
explanation.definitionFit: A gullible dupe is easily cheated, so such a person pays too much.

clue.text: Brand new acceptable sculpture of nudes

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, hence socially acceptable

indicators.note: a sculpture shapes material anew, so the letters of nudes are remodelled

explanation.surface: A fresh, decent statue of naked figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never yet employed is pristine, as good as new.
